claim: Source and documentation review of ossf/scorecard at commit f92023a3f77879f96e0c9c1305f289d755be4bb6 (license Apache-2.0), read from README.md at that commit. Repository description: "OpenSSF Scorecard - Security health metrics for Open Source". Reviewer summary of the upstream documentation: OpenSSF's automated security-health scorer for open-source repos: ~18 checks (Token-Permissions, Pinned-Dependencies, Branch-Protection, Vulnerabilities, etc.), each scored 0-10, with a first-party GitHub Action (ossf/scorecard-action) that publishes results to the repo's code-scanning/Security tab. Requirement part it addresses (ci-supply-chain): Directly serves 'scoped workflow permissions' via its Token-Permissions check (least-privilege GITHUB_TOKEN scoring: top-level read-only = max score, job-level-only declarations lose a point) and 'attributable hosted checks' via scorecard-action's continuous, code-scanning-integrated run.

documentation_excerpts.text: - Default Scorecard Checks - Detailed Check Documentation (Scoring Criteria, Risks, and Remediation) - Beginner's Guide to Scorecard Checks

Scorecard is an automated tool that assesses a number of important heuristics ("checks") associated with software security and assigns each check a score of 0-10. You can use these scores to understand specific areas to improve in order to strengthen the security posture of your project.

limitations: Source and documentation review at the pinned commit only: not installed, executed, benchmarked or compared with any other component.

The description and excerpts are the upstream project's own words at that commit; the reviewer summary was written by a research agent and checked by an independent fit review. Both are upstream claims, not measured results.
